about: The content-intelligence playbook: platforms, pillars, segments and the sports calendar. `priors` are STARTING HYPOTHESES (1 = poor fit, 5 = strong fit) from how each platform distributes video, not measurements. outputs/content_intel.py replaces them with your own results as posts are logged (content intel log / import). Edit freely; run `content intel segments` to check it parses.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.drivers: Completion and rewatches decide distribution; shares and saves are the strongest signals after that. The first 2 seconds decide whether anyone sees the rest.
tiktok.packaging: Burn in captions. Put the claim on screen in the first frame. Keep the bottom 420 px and right 180 px clear (the booth's TikTok guide shows them).
tiktok.policy: TikTok does not allow promoting gambling services: no sportsbook logos, promo codes, odds-boost screens or links to books. Analysis and education are fine, but gambling-adjacent videos can be held out of For You, so lead with the sport, not the bet.

shorts.label: YouTube Shorts
shorts.drivers: Viewed-versus-swiped-away and average percentage viewed. Loops count, so a clean ending that flows into the start helps. Subscribers from Shorts feed the long-form channel.
shorts.packaging: Title is the hook in under 60 characters. Keep the bottom 400 px clear. Link the related long-form video.
shorts.policy: YouTube limits content that promises returns or points viewers to unapproved gambling sites, and gambling content can earn limited ads. Never promise winnings; do not say or show sportsbook URLs or promo codes.

x.label: X
x.drivers: Replies, reposts and quote posts, bookmarks, then dwell. Video autoplays muted, so captions carry it. The betting community lives here and argues about lines, so takes and line moves travel.
x.packaging: Write the post text so it stands alone without the video. Put links in a reply, not the main post. A 3-post thread (video, the key number, the link) works for longer breakdowns.
x.policy: Paid promotion of gambling is restricted. Organic analysis is fine. Same rule as everywhere: no guarantees.

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.drivers: Click-through on the thumbnail and title, then average view duration. Chapters help search and retention. Series and playlists bring viewers back.
post_windows_et: the evening before the slate (Fri for CFB, Sat for NFL)
youtube.packaging: Title under 70 characters, front-load the game or topic. Make the thumbnail with thumbnail.bat. Paste the booth's chapters.txt into the description. Cut 2-3 Shorts from the strongest chapters.
youtube.policy: Same as Shorts. Keep a responsible-gambling line in the description.

timely.label: Game breakdowns
timely.why: Game-week content is what people search for and share before kickoff. It also shows off the site.

education.label: Betting education
education.why: Evergreen, saved and shared, and it builds trust. It keeps working after the week ends.

trading.label: Sports trading
trading.why: Lines as prices: movement, timing and hedging. A fresh angle most betting accounts do not cover well.

modeling.label: Matchup modeling
modeling.why: How the numbers are built. This sets Chase Analytics apart from accounts that just post picks.

community.label: Results & community
community.why: Report cards and answering comments keep the audience coming back and make the account accountable.

cadence.about: Recordings per weekday. One vertical take is cut for TikTok, Shorts and X; one wide take is the YouTube long-form video. Start here, then raise what the results reward.

learning.about: A post's score is its lift over your typical post on that platform (log ratio, weighted by the platform's metric_weights). Each segment starts at its prior, worth `prior_strength` posts, and moves toward your real results as they arrive. Segments with few posts get an `explore` bonus so everything gets tried. A segment stops being planned for a platform once it has `drop_after` posts there and still scores below `drop_below`.

compliance.about: `never` phrases are false promises and must not appear. `platform_risk` phrases read as promoting a gambling service, which TikTok and YouTube suppress or remove.
